_meta.not_included: Homepage is only a navigation hub (no transport data). Louage data is in louage_tunisia.json. The international ferry page and the covid travel page were not fetched.
_meta.caveat: The source is a tourist blog fed by reader comments. Fares and timetables can be stale; always keep the source date and check the operator site (links in each section).

taxi.description: City taxis. All yellow, with a roof number and a meter, in every town, at almost any hour.
taxi.availability_light: Windshield light: red = free, green = occupied (as stated by the source).
restrictions: Cannot leave their own city (e.g. no Tunis-Hammamet by yellow taxi).
Max 3 adults; a 4th passenger is tolerated only if under 10 years old.
how_to: Hail anywhere with a raised hand, after checking the light shows free.
Custom: men sit in front, women in back; board from the right (left door is locked).
State the destination and check the meter starts at 0.

tariff_dec_2022.pricing_model: Per ride in big cities; per person (shared ride, can board an occupied taxi) in smaller towns.

tips: Avoid office hours in big cities.
Easier to find a taxi on popular streets than on major arteries.
At Tunis airport, go up to the departures level and hail a taxi that just dropped someone off; waiting taxis below quote inflated fares.
Chatting with the driver and showing you know the area reduces scam risk.
scams_reported_rare: Taking a longer route (check road signs).
Charging per person at 3x the meter, or quoting a flat price at the start.

other_taxi_types.description: Larger white taxi that can go anywhere in Tunisia. Fares are described as exorbitant for most people.
other_taxi_types.example: About 50 TND for airport to Hammamet (airport page).

other_taxi_types.description: Shared taxi on fixed corridors in Tunis, priced per seat (see observed fares).

fare_observations.note: 17 TND on the meter plus luggage/airport supplement.
Looks high relative to the neighbouring entry; verify.
Quoted 45 EUR, negotiated to 35 EUR; this is a private taxi, in euros.

tunis_tram_metro.naming: Locals call it the Métro, but it is a surface tramway (not underground).

network.network_note: Figures from the page (2024); the network is under almost constant extension.
network.rolling_stock: Citadis trams since 2007, running alongside older trains.

fares.model: Zone-based, paid at a gated station area.

tips: Overcrowded at office hours; very popular with urban buses.

tgm.description: Suburban rail hybrid (not exactly tram, metro or train) running from central Tunis to La Goulette, Carthage, Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa.

notable_stops: Sidi Bou Saïd (about 3 min walk to the village)

tgm.airport_stop_warning: A TGM stop is named 'Aéroport' but it is NOT at Tunis-Carthage airport (historical leftover). No rail reaches the airport.
tgm.frequency: About 20 minutes between trains, depending on time of day.

fares.note: Depends on distance and class; source says about 20x cheaper than a taxi for a similar trip.

tgm.crowding: Kram/Tunis section packed during office hours.
tgm.history: First trains in 1872; electrified since 1908. Connection projects to the tram network keep being discussed.

national_rail.operator: SNCFT (Société Nationale des Chemins de Fer Tunisiens)

network.main_axis: Tunis - Hammamet - Sousse - El Jem - Sfax - Gabès (east coast)
network.dead_link: The former line to Algeria is out of service (viaducts remain near Béja).

rolling_stock.description: Most modern trains, single class like French TER, good condition. Used mainly between Sousse and Tunis (2h20).
Older trains, 3 classes: Seconde, Première, Confort. Confort recommended (calmer, slightly pricier). Rolling stock is dated; probably air-conditioned but bring water in summer.

reliability: Trains usually depart on time but often arrive late.
Intermediate stops may still be served even if the official time has passed.
Old track and level-crossing accidents regularly cause delays.

fares.rule_of_thumb: About 6-7 TND per hour of travel in Confort class (close to louage prices).
fares.online_tickets: Possible via SNCFT (not tested by the source).

stations.name: Gare de Tunis (Barcelone)
stations.location_note: Place Barcelone, about 300 m south of Avenue Habib Bourguiba. Reachable on foot, by taxi or tram. Ask taxis for 'Barchelone'.
stations.services: Departure point for urban and national lines; ticket needed to access platforms; left-luggage office on the left when entering.

stations.name: National station
stations.location_note: About 400 m north-east of the medina (also described as in the city centre, about 100 m from the medina on the route page). Small station with a snack on the outside wall. About 5 minutes on foot to the medina walls.
stations.note: Louage station in Sousse is out of the centre.

stations.name: Métro du Sahel station
stations.location_note: About 400 m south-east of the medina.

stations.name: Sfax station
stations.location_note: About 500 m north-east of the medina, in the colonial quarter. Walk south to reach the municipality building and the Bab Diwan esplanade.

stations.name: Hammamet station (Bir Bou Regba)
stations.location_note: Several km from the beaches and tourist area; a taxi is needed to reach Hammamet.

route_notes.note: About one train per hour; good in summer to avoid traffic jams, but the station is far from the beach.
Excellent option between these two cities.

route_notes.route: Tunis - El Jem, then Mahdia - Tunis (weekend idea)
route_notes.note: Express at 07:35 from Tunis arrives El Jem about 11:30. Then louage El Jem to Mahdia (about 1 h). Return to Tunis by louage.
Only one train each way per day; night trains no longer run.

metro_du_sahel.description: A commuter train (not a metro) linking Sousse, Monastir and Mahdia, about 2 hours end to end, about 30 stations. Electrified, recent and comfortable (unlike the main network).

lezard_rouge.description: Historic tourist train at Metlaoui (between Gafsa and Tozeur), dated 1924, running through a gorge to phosphate quarries.
lezard_rouge.status: Out of service since the 2010 floods; reopening announced every year, still uncertain in 2025.

kerkennah_ferry.route: Sfax - Kerkennah islands (only transport to the island)
kerkennah_ferry.operator: SONOTRAK (Société Nouvelle de Transport de Kerkennah)
kerkennah_ferry.info_phone_note: Automatic voice recorder giving the day's timetable.

terminals.sfax: Large white building on the railway line, near the Sfax train station and the International Fair (look for the SONOTRAK sign).

schedule.frequency: A boat every 1h to 1h30 during the day, both directions.
schedule.seasonality: Times vary by season; more sailings in summer, especially early and late in the day.

fares.note: Check the official site for the full tariff.

boarding.pedestrians: Buy tickets at the counter inside the terminal.
boarding.cars: Pay at the gate when entering; queue along the railway line. Vehicles enter at the bow and exit at the stern (some boats have a single door, so reverse in).

reservations.note: Only 20 vehicle spots can be reserved; they go fast, especially on weekends. Weekend-evening returns to Sfax are very busy.

tips: Arrive early to find the terminal and get a good queue position.
Reserve both outbound and return in summer and on Sundays.
Best time for the islands: summer, but autumn to spring is quiet and less touristy.

tunis_carthage_airport.name: Tunis-Carthage airport
tunis_carthage_airport.rail_access: None (the TGM stop named 'Aéroport' is not at the airport).

taxi_yellow_estimates_tnd.to: Carthage / La Marsa / Sidi Bou Saïd

tunis_carthage_airport.taxi_tip: Go up to the departures level and take a taxi leaving after a drop-off; make sure the meter runs (no supplement in that case).

to_hammamet.info: Bus stop is on the right when exiting the airport. Operator site: http://www.srtgn.com.tn/site/ih_action.php

to_hammamet.note: Taxi to Bab Alioua station, then louage or bus.

tunis_carthage_airport.drop_off: Dépose-minute on the departures level, 10 m from the check-in hall; police forbid stopping there.
tunis_carthage_airport.left_luggage: None known at the airport; use the left-luggage office at Tunis train station.
tunis_carthage_airport.sim_cards: Tunisie Télécom, Ooredoo and Orange have shops at the airport; SIM about 5 TND.

other_modes_overview.description: Each region has its own bus network. Schedules are respected, vehicles often good, fares very low.
Many agencies; cars of fairly good quality; economical when several people travel; gives autonomy. Rental desks are in the arrivals hall at Tunis airport.
8 airports in Tunisia served by Tunisair and Tunisair Express; much faster, but expensive.

interchange_notes: Tunis Marine (end of Avenue Bourguiba) is the TGM terminus.
Tunis train station (place Barcelone) is about 300 m south of Avenue Habib Bourguiba and reachable by tram.
Bab Alioua louage station (Cap Bon / Hammamet) is the usual taxi transfer from the airport for Hammamet.
Sousse train station is close to the medina; the louage station is out of the centre.
Hammamet train station (Bir Bou Regba) is several km from the beaches; plan a taxi.
Monastir airport is served by the Métro du Sahel.
Sfax ferry terminal is next to the railway line and train station.
modeling_notes_not_from_source: TGM, tram and ferry are frequency-based services: model headways (TGM about 20 min, ferry 60-90 min) rather than fixed timetables unless you import official ones.
Yellow taxis can be modeled with the tariff formula (0.9 + 0.6/km + 0.15/min, +50% at night) but are restricted to the city: do not use them for inter-city edges.
Train timetables on the page are sparse and dated 2025; import official SNCFT data instead if you can.
For hubs, add walking/taxi transfer edges (for example Tunis train station to Avenue Bourguiba, Bir Bou Regba to Hammamet).
